doc.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]

title: The future of jazz and women at the jazz party
summary: Hyman praises the inclusion of Nicki Parrott, Karol Strassmayer and Sherrie Maricle.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Yeah. You can really tell if you’re watching him. It’s like this is a weird thing to do. Well this has been a great conversation again. Just to wrap up, you’ve seen jazz — jazz changes so fast, it’s just amazing.

And I just wonder where is it going? How can it keep changing so fast? Do you have any opinions on what’s going to happen with it? When I look at this jazz party scene, it’s really wonderful to be at, I wonder how long it can keep going.
One of the most remarkable things about this party is the way that Mat [Domber] has been including women. And that bass player, what’s her name, Parrott, Vicky is her name?
Nicki Parrott. Wonderful — and I saw the saxophonist is that Strassmayer?
Karol Strassmayer. She was terrific last night. And the drummer.

Sherrie Maricle. Terrific. I realize that really we have been neglecting a great resource. And this is the first party, the first casting I’ve seen in which these terrific players are represented without being an all-girl band and which is kind of an insulting thing anyhow. So I’m happy to see that. Where the music is going I don’t know. Who can possibly say? I find that I’m less interested in such conjectures and just trying to concentrate on where I’m going.
